tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"

    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)

    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)

    height_inches : float

    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):

tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing QTc value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)
    Bazett: QTc = QT / √(RR)
    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)
    Hodges M, et al. J Electrocardiol. 1983;16(1):17-24
    Rautaharju PM, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(3):594-600

tool_list.name: ibw_abw_calculator
tool_list.description:
Ideal Body Weight and Adjusted Body Weight Calculator
    Calculates ideal body weight (Devine formula) and adjusted body weight.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    weight_kg : float
        Actual body weight in kilograms
    height_inches : float
        Height in inches
    male : bool
        True if patient is male, False if female
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):
    - Men: IBW = 50 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    - Women: IBW = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    
    Adjusted Body Weight (ABW):
    - ABW = IBW + 0.4 × (actual weight - IBW)
    
    References:
    -----------
    Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm. 1974;8:650-655.
    Pai MP. Drug Dosing Based on Weight and Body Surface Area: Mathematical Assumptions and Limitations in Obese Adults. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(9):856-868.

        Method used for calculation: "lmp" (last menstrual period), "conception", or "ultrasound"
    date_value : str
        Date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD' (date of LMP, conception, or ultrasound)
    cycle_length : int, optional
        Length of menstrual cycle in days (default: 28)
    gestational_age_weeks : int, optional
        Weeks of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    gestational_age_days : int, optional
        Days of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing calculated pregnancy dates and information
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    - EGA (Estimated Gestational Age) = time since 1st day of LMP
    - EDC (Estimated Date of Conception) = LMP + 2 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    - EDD (Estimated Due Date) = LMP + 40 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    
    For non-28 day cycles:
    - Adjustment = (cycle_length - 28) days
    - EDD = LMP + 40 weeks + Adjustment

tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing QTc value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)
    Bazett: QTc = QT / √(RR)
    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)
    Hodges M, et al. J Electrocardiol. 1983;16(1):17-24
    Rautaharju PM, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(3):594-600

tool_list.description:
Ideal Body Weight and Adjusted Body Weight Calculator
    Calculates ideal body weight (Devine formula) and adjusted body weight.
    
    Parameters:

    weight_kg : float
        Actual body weight in kilograms
    height_inches : float
        Height in inches
    male : bool
        True if patient is male, False if female
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):
    - Men: IBW = 50 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    - Women: IBW = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)

    References:
    -----------
    Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm. 1974;8:650-655.
    Pai MP. Drug Dosing Based on Weight and Body Surface Area: Mathematical Assumptions and Limitations in Obese Adults. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(9):856-868.

question:
I’m seeing a 50-year-old man with serum creatinine 1.0 mg/dL. He’s a current smoker, no diabetes, SBP 138 mmHg, and he’s taking an antihypertensive but not on a statin. Lipids today: total cholesterol 5.2 mmol/L and HDL 1.3 mmol/L.
    
    Can you (1) calculate his eGFR from the creatinine and age/sex, then (2) use that eGFR to calculate his 10-year CVD risk with the PREVENT model (include the risk category), and (3) also calculate his 10-year Framingham heart attack risk and tell me how the two risk estimates compare?
extract_agent_text_text:
### 1) eGFR (2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation)
- **Inputs:** 50-year-old man, Scr **1.0 mg/dL**
- **eGFR:** **91.7 mL/min/1.73 m²**

---

### 2) PREVENT 10-year CVD risk (using that eGFR)
- **Inputs used:** age 50, male, **TC 5.2 mmol/L**, **HDL 1.3 mmol/L**, **SBP 138**, **current smoker**, **no diabetes**, **on antihypertensive**, **not on statin**, **eGFR 91.7**
- **10-year CVD risk:** **7.8%**
- **Risk category:** **Intermediate**

---

### 3) 10-year Framingham “heart attack” (CHD) risk + comparison
- (Framingham tool uses mg/dL; converted: TC ≈ **201 mg/dL**, HDL ≈ **50 mg/dL**)
- **10-year Framingham heart attack (CHD) risk:** **15.05%**

**How they compare**
- **Framingham (15.1%) is higher than PREVENT (7.8%)**, roughly about **2× higher**.
- They’re not estimating exactly the same outcome: **PREVENT = broader CVD events**, while **Framingham here is framed as “heart attack/CHD” risk**; also the underlying cohorts and calibration differ, so absolute percentages can diverge even with similar inputs.

tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing QTc value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)
    Bazett: QTc = QT / √(RR)
    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)
    Hodges M, et al. J Electrocardiol. 1983;16(1):17-24
    Rautaharju PM, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(3):594-600

tool_list.name: ibw_abw_calculator
tool_list.description:
Ideal Body Weight and Adjusted Body Weight Calculator
    Calculates ideal body weight (Devine formula) and adjusted body weight.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    weight_kg : float
        Actual body weight in kilograms
    height_inches : float
        Height in inches
    male : bool
        True if patient is male, False if female
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):
    - Men: IBW = 50 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    - Women: IBW = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    
    Adjusted Body Weight (ABW):
    - ABW = IBW + 0.4 × (actual weight - IBW)
    
    References:
    -----------
    Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm. 1974;8:650-655.
    Pai MP. Drug Dosing Based on Weight and Body Surface Area: Mathematical Assumptions and Limitations in Obese Adults. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(9):856-868.

tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing QTc value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)
    Bazett: QTc = QT / √(RR)
    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)
    Hodges M, et al. J Electrocardiol. 1983;16(1):17-24
    Rautaharju PM, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(3):594-600

tool_list.name: ibw_abw_calculator
tool_list.description:
Ideal Body Weight and Adjusted Body Weight Calculator
    Calculates ideal body weight (Devine formula) and adjusted body weight.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    weight_kg : float
        Actual body weight in kilograms
    height_inches : float
        Height in inches
    male : bool
        True if patient is male, False if female
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):
    - Men: IBW = 50 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    - Women: IBW = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    
    Adjusted Body Weight (ABW):
    - ABW = IBW + 0.4 × (actual weight - IBW)
    
    References:
    -----------
    Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm. 1974;8:650-655.
    Pai MP. Drug Dosing Based on Weight and Body Surface Area: Mathematical Assumptions and Limitations in Obese Adults. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(9):856-868.

        Method used for calculation: "lmp" (last menstrual period), "conception", or "ultrasound"
    date_value : str
        Date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD' (date of LMP, conception, or ultrasound)
    cycle_length : int, optional
        Length of menstrual cycle in days (default: 28)
    gestational_age_weeks : int, optional
        Weeks of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    gestational_age_days : int, optional
        Days of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")

    dict
        Dictionary containing calculated pregnancy dates and information

    ---------
    - EGA (Estimated Gestational Age) = time since 1st day of LMP
    - EDC (Estimated Date of Conception) = LMP + 2 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    - EDD (Estimated Due Date) = LMP + 40 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)

    - Adjustment = (cycle_length - 28) days
    - EDD = LMP + 40 weeks + Adjustment

question:
I’m counseling a 50-year-old man with no known cardiovascular disease. His serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL. Vitals/labs: SBP 135 mmHg (he’s on antihypertensives), total cholesterol 200 mg/dL, HDL 45 mg/dL. He’s a current smoker and has diabetes; he’s also already taking a statin.
    
    Can you (1) calculate his eGFR, then (2) use that eGFR to estimate his 10-year CVD risk using the PREVENT model (please use the lipids in mmol/L, so convert from the mg/dL values), and (3) also calculate his 10-year Framingham CHD risk so I can compare the two estimates?
extract_agent_text_text:
### 1) eGFR (2021 CKD-EPI creatinine equation)
Inputs: male, age 50, Scr 1.0 mg/dL  
**eGFR ≈ 91.7 mL/min/1.73 m²**

---

### 2) PREVENT 10-year CVD risk (using lipids in mmol/L, and using the eGFR above)
**Convert lipids (mg/dL → mmol/L):**
- Total cholesterol: 200 mg/dL × 0.02586 = **5.172 mmol/L**
- HDL: 45 mg/dL × 0.02586 = **1.165 mmol/L**

Inputs used: age 50, male, TC 5.172, HDL 1.165, SBP 135 (on antihypertensives), diabetes yes, current smoker yes, **eGFR 91.7**, on statin yes.  
**PREVENT 10-year CVD risk: 16.3%** (category: **Intermediate**)

---

### 3) Framingham 10-year CHD risk (for comparison)
Inputs: male, age 50, TC 200 mg/dL, HDL 45 mg/dL, SBP 135 (treated), smoker yes.  
**Framingham 10-year CHD risk: 15.92%**

---

If you want, I can also compute a 10-year **ASCVD Pooled Cohort** estimate (commonly used in US guidelines) to triangulate alongside PREVENT and Framingham.

Ideal Body Weight and Adjusted Body Weight Calculator
    Calculates ideal body weight (Devine formula) and adjusted body weight.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    weight_kg : float
        Actual body weight in kilograms
    height_inches : float
        Height in inches
    male : bool
        True if patient is male, False if female
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):
    - Men: IBW = 50 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    - Women: IBW = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    
    Adjusted Body Weight (ABW):
    - ABW = IBW + 0.4 × (actual weight - IBW)
    
    References:
    -----------
    Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm. 1974;8:650-655.
    Pai MP. Drug Dosing Based on Weight and Body Surface Area: Mathematical Assumptions and Limitations in Obese Adults. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(9):856-868.

tool_list.name: pregnancy_calculator
tool_list.description:
Pregnancy Due Dates Calculator
    Calculates pregnancy dates from last period, gestational age, or date of conception.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    calculation_method : str
        Method used for calculation: "lmp" (last menstrual period), "conception", or "ultrasound"
    date_value : str
        Date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD' (date of LMP, conception, or ultrasound)
    cycle_length : int, optional
        Length of menstrual cycle in days (default: 28)
    gestational_age_weeks : int, optional
        Weeks of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    gestational_age_days : int, optional
        Days of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing calculated pregnancy dates and information
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    - EGA (Estimated Gestational Age) = time since 1st day of LMP
    - EDC (Estimated Date of Conception) = LMP + 2 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    - EDD (Estimated Due Date) = LMP + 40 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    
    For non-28 day cycles:
    - Adjustment = (cycle_length - 28) days
    - EDD = LMP + 40 weeks + Adjustment

question:
I’m reconciling renal function estimates for medication dosing vs CKD staging in a 50-year-old man with serum creatinine 1.0 mg/dL and cystatin C 1.1 mg/L. He’s 5'10" (70 inches) and weighs 95 kg. 
    Can you calculate (1) eGFR using the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine-only equation, (2) eGFR using the 2021 CKD-EPI creatinine+cystatin C equation, and (3) Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance—and then briefly compare the three numbers and indicate which one is typically used for drug dosing?
extract_agent_text_text:
### 1) eGFR (2021 CKD-EPI creatinine-only)
- **eGFR ≈ 91.7 mL/min/1.73 m²**

### 2) eGFR (2021 CKD-EPI creatinine + cystatin C)
- **eGFR ≈ 81.8 mL/min/1.73 m²**

### 3) Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance (CrCl)
- **CrCl ≈ 102.2 mL/min**
  - (Calculator used **adjusted body weight** because of elevated body weight: **IBW ~73.0 kg**, **AdjBW ~81.8 kg**)

---

## Brief comparison / interpretation
- The two **eGFR values** are **indexed to body surface area (1.73 m²)** and are primarily used for **CKD staging** and clinical assessment.
- The **combined creatinine+cystatin C eGFR (81.8)** is **lower** than creatinine-only eGFR (91.7), which commonly happens when cystatin C suggests slightly lower filtration than creatinine alone.
- **Cockcroft–Gault CrCl (102.2 mL/min)** is **not BSA-indexed** and often runs **higher** than eGFR, especially depending on weight choice (actual vs ideal vs adjusted).

## Which is typically used for drug dosing?
- **Most drug labels and many hospital dosing protocols still use Cockcroft–Gault CrCl** for renal dose adjustment **unless the specific drug guidance says to use eGFR** (some newer guidance/protocols use CKD-EPI eGFR).
- Best practice: **follow the dosing method specified in the drug’s prescribing information / protocol** (CrCl vs eGFR, and whether to use actual/ideal/adjusted weight for CG).

tool_list.name: corrected_calcium
tool_list.description:
Calcium Correction for Hypoalbuminemia and Hyperalbuminemia
    Calculates a corrected calcium level for patients with abnormal albumin levels.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    serum_calcium : float
        Patient's measured serum calcium level in mg/dL
    patient_albumin : float
        Patient's serum albumin level in g/dL
    normal_albumin : float, optional
        Normal/reference albumin level in g/dL, default is 4.0 g/dL
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing corrected calcium value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formula:
    --------
    Corrected Calcium = (0.8 * (Normal Albumin - Patient's Albumin)) + Serum Calcium
    
    References:
    -----------
    Payne RB, et al. Br Med J. 1973;4(5893):643-646.

tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing QTc value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)
    Bazett: QTc = QT / √(RR)
    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)
    Hodges M, et al. J Electrocardiol. 1983;16(1):17-24
    Rautaharju PM, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(3):594-600

question:
A 54-year-old woman with known cirrhosis comes to clinic. Her labs today are: total bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL, albumin 2.7 g/dL, INR 1.9, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, sodium 128 mEq/L. Clinically she has moderate ascites and mild hepatic encephalopathy (grade 1–2). She has not had dialysis in the last week.
    
    Can you calculate both her Child-Pugh score and her MELD 3.0 score from these values, and summarize what each score implies about severity/risk?
extract_agent_text_text:
## Child–Pugh score (cirrhosis severity)

**Inputs → points**
- **Total bilirubin 3.1 mg/dL** → **3 points** (>\*3)
- **Albumin 2.7 g/dL** → **3 points** (<2.8)
- **INR 1.9** → **2 points** (1.7–2.3)
- **Ascites: moderate** → **3 points**
- **Encephalopathy: mild (grade 1–2)** → **2 points**

**Total Child–Pugh = 3 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 13**

**Class:** **Child–Pugh C** (10–15)

**What it implies:** **Decompensated, severe cirrhosis** with higher short-term mortality risk and complications; typically supports **urgent hepatology management and transplant evaluation** (if otherwise eligible).

---

## MELD 3.0 score (short-term mortality / transplant priority)

Using age 54, female, bilirubin 3.1, INR 1.9, creatinine 1.4, albumin 2.7, sodium 128, **no dialysis**:

**MELD 3.0 = 28**

**What it implies:** A **high MELD** indicating **significant 90-day mortality risk** in advanced liver disease and generally **higher priority for liver transplant listing** relative to lower MELD values (exact waitlist priority depends on local allocation and exceptions).

---

### Quick interpretation summary
- **Child–Pugh 13 (Class C):** overall **clinical decompensation/severity** (ascites + encephalopathy heavily influence this).
- **MELD 3.0 28:** **high short-term mortality risk** used for **transplant urgency/allocation** (driven here notably by **hyponatremia**, INR, bilirubin, low albumin, and renal function).

tool_list.name: qtc_calculator
tool_list.description:
Corrected QT Interval (QTc) Calculator
    Corrects the QT interval for heart rate extremes using various formulas.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    qt_interval : float
        Measured QT interval in milliseconds (ms)
    heart_rate : float
        Heart rate in beats per minute (bpm)
    formula : str, optional
        Formula to use for correction (default: "bazett")
        Options: "bazett", "fridericia", "framingham", "hodges", "rautaharju"
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing QTc value, interpretation, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    RR interval = 60 / heart_rate (in seconds)
    Bazett: QTc = QT / √(RR)
    Fridericia: QTc = QT / (RR)^(1/3)
    Framingham: QTc = QT + 154 × (1 - RR)
    Hodges: QTc = QT + 1.75 × (heart_rate - 60)
    Rautaharju: QTc = QT × (120 + heart_rate) / 180
    
    References:
    -----------
    Bazett HC. Heart. 1920;7:353-370
    Fridericia LS. Acta Med Scand. 1920;53:469-486
    Sagie A, et al. Am J Cardiol. 1992;70(7):797-801 (Framingham)
    Hodges M, et al. J Electrocardiol. 1983;16(1):17-24
    Rautaharju PM, et al. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2004;44(3):594-600

tool_list.name: ibw_abw_calculator
tool_list.description:
Ideal Body Weight and Adjusted Body Weight Calculator
    Calculates ideal body weight (Devine formula) and adjusted body weight.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    weight_kg : float
        Actual body weight in kilograms
    height_inches : float
        Height in inches
    male : bool
        True if patient is male, False if female
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing ideal body weight, adjusted body weight, and calculation details
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    Ideal Body Weight (IBW) (Devine formula):
    - Men: IBW = 50 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    - Women: IBW = 45.5 kg + 2.3 kg × (height in inches - 60)
    
    Adjusted Body Weight (ABW):
    - ABW = IBW + 0.4 × (actual weight - IBW)
    
    References:
    -----------
    Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm. 1974;8:650-655.
    Pai MP. Drug Dosing Based on Weight and Body Surface Area: Mathematical Assumptions and Limitations in Obese Adults. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(9):856-868.

tool_list.description:
Pregnancy Due Dates Calculator
    Calculates pregnancy dates from last period, gestational age, or date of conception.
    
    Parameters:
    -----------
    calculation_method : str
        Method used for calculation: "lmp" (last menstrual period), "conception", or "ultrasound"
    date_value : str
        Date in format 'YYYY-MM-DD' (date of LMP, conception, or ultrasound)
    cycle_length : int, optional
        Length of menstrual cycle in days (default: 28)
    gestational_age_weeks : int, optional
        Weeks of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    gestational_age_days : int, optional
        Days of gestational age at ultrasound (required if calculation_method is "ultrasound")
    
    Returns:
    --------
    dict
        Dictionary containing calculated pregnancy dates and information
        
    Formulas:
    ---------
    - EGA (Estimated Gestational Age) = time since 1st day of LMP
    - EDC (Estimated Date of Conception) = LMP + 2 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    - EDD (Estimated Due Date) = LMP + 40 weeks (adjusted for cycle length)
    
    For non-28 day cycles:
    - Adjustment = (cycle_length - 28) days
    - EDD = LMP + 40 weeks + Adjustment
